subject.title: fix(llm): summarize ephemeral tool results to preserve prefix cache

question: Which tool-result visibility policy should OpenClaw use for DeepSeek prefix-cache preservation: narrow heartbeat/status placeholders, a broader ephemeral-tool policy, or an isolated-session/cache-boundary strategy instead?
rationale: The code can preserve provider call-result pairing either way, but deciding which tool outputs may be hidden from model-visible context affects agent reasoning, session state, and provider-cache behavior, so code inspection alone cannot safely choose the permanent policy.

options.title: Narrow to low-value status results
options.body: Only summarize maintainer-approved heartbeat/status outputs, leave normal `exec`, `read`, web, and memory results model-visible, and keep the linked issue open until live DeepSeek proof covers the chosen scope.

options.title: Use an isolation/cache-boundary strategy
options.body: Avoid hiding tool outputs and instead rely on isolated heartbeat sessions, context pruning, or the related boundary-cache work for provider-cache preservation.

options.title: Accept broad result hiding explicitly
options.body: Document and test a broad policy that selected normal tools no longer feed their outputs back to the model, accepting the agent-reasoning compatibility impact.

recommendation.title: Narrow to low-value status results
recommendation.body: Only summarize maintainer-approved heartbeat/status outputs, leave normal `exec`, `read`, web, and memory results model-visible, and keep the linked issue open until live DeepSeek proof covers the chosen scope.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest prompt-cache boundary history and is the best available routing owner for the provider-cache policy decision.
